messages.content: I need to make a couple of hotel reservations. First, secure a room for 2 adults and 1 child at the Sheraton Hotel in New York with check-in on May 1, 2022, and check-out on May 5, 2022. Then, reserve a room for 1 adult and 2 children at the Marriott in Los Angeles, checking in on June 1, 2022, and checking out on June 10, 2022.

function.name: hotel_booking_book
function.description: Book a hotel room at the specified location for the specified number of adults and children, ensuring the accommodation dates are available. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

hotel_name.description: The name of the hotel to book.

location.description: The location of the hotel, in the format of 'City, State', such as 'San Francisco, CA' or 'New York, NY'.

check_in.description: The check-in date for the booking, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

check_out.description: The check-out date for the booking, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

adults.description: The number of adults included in the booking.

children.description: The number of children included in the booking.

message.reasoning: The user wants to book two hotel rooms. We have a function to call: hotel_booking_book. We need to call it twice with the appropriate arguments. The function expects check_in and check_out in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. The user gave dates in words: May 1, 2022 -> 2022-05-01. May 5, 2022 -> 2022-05-05. June 1, 2022 -> 2022-06-01. June 10, 2022 -> 2022-06-10. The user also gave the hotel names: Sheraton Hotel in New York, Marriott in Los Angeles. The location format: 'City, State'. For New York, we can use 'New York, NY'. For Los Angeles, 'Los Angeles, CA'. The user didn't specify the state for New York but we can assume NY. The user didn't specify the city for Marriott but we can assume Los Angeles. The user didn't specify the number of adults and children: 2 adults, 1 child for Sheraton; 1 adult, 2 children for Marriott. So we need to call the function twice. The function returns any. We need to output the function calls. The user didn't ask for anything else. So we just call the function twice.
